newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House Democrats press SEC on utility rulings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House Democrats press SEC on utility rulings.

text.p: Two key U.S. House Democrats raised concern in a letter released Monday that the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) might be ignoring consumer protections under the Public Utility Holding Company Act.

Representatives Ed Markey of Massachusetts and John Dingell of Michigan asked the SEC to outline action it was taking on plans by gas and electric utilities Entergy Corp, The Southern Company, and Consolidated Natural Gas Co to move into businesses outside their core areas.
The two House members, senior Democrats on the House Commerce Committee, will be key players in debates expected next year on breaking electric utility monopolies.
"We're following up on the concerns that we expressed in our April letter, that the commission by its actions appears to moving toward administratively repealing PUHCA," said an aide to Markey.
"We do not believe that PUHCA can be safely eliminated without proceeding far more comprehensively with restructuring the electricity industry," he said.
The 60-year-old law was designed to protect utility customers and shareholders from subsidizing electric utility holding companies' unprofitable attempts to diversify.

The lawmakers in their September 25 letter urged the SEC to hold a hearing on its contested order issued earlier this year that allowed Southern Co to invest all of its retained earnings in foreign utilities.

"... (W)e question whether the Commission's interpretation ... upholds the statutory requirements that such diversification be permitted only if it is demonstrated that it will not adversely affect the compahy's financial integrity or the interests of its electricity customers," they said.
The SEC last year issued a report calling for repeal of PUHCA, saying it was no longer needed because other regulators were authorized to shield utility consumers.
The SEC had no comment on the exchange of letters.
